- mod.rs routes 0x060-0x07F and 0x090-0x09F to psg.rs and steps it with `psg.step(cycles)`. Keep that.

- Events in gba.rs, already wired by the integrator:
  - On every timer overflow, gba.rs calls `apu.on_timer_overflow(timer_index) -> u8`. Return the bit mask of FIFOs (bit 0 = A, bit 1 = B) that need a refill, i.e. holding 16 bytes or fewer (gbatek), and gba.rs forwards that to `dma.notify_fifo_request(fifo)`.

# gba-emu: rules for every agent

Read PLAN.md before starting. It defines the phases, the shared contracts and who owns which file.
The benchmark lives at `/var/www/html/test-projects/gba-eval`, referred to below as `$GBA_EVAL`.
Use that absolute path; relative paths break inside worktrees.

## Originality (hard rule)
- Write all code yourself. Do not read, copy, or paraphrase any existing emulator:
  `$GBA_EVAL/candidates/` (gba-core), `$GBA_EVAL/third_party/` (Mesen2),
  `$GBA_EVAL/reference/mesen_step.cpp`, or mGBA/NanoBoyAdvance/VBA/etc. from memory or the web.
- Allowed sources: `$GBA_EVAL/spec/gbatek.htm` (GBA, ARM and THUMB chapters only), `$GBA_EVAL/spec/ABI.md`,
  `$GBA_EVAL/spec/gba_bios_stub.h`, the grader's outputs (scores, `.ref.png` vs `.cand.png`),
  and running ROMs from `$GBA_EVAL/corpus/roms/`.
- No per-ROM hacks: never branch on a ROM's hash, title, or game code. Fix the hardware behavior.

## Code readability
- Use clear, descriptive names for functions, variables and types: `destination_register`, `shift_amount`,
  `fn execute_data_processing`. Never cryptic ones like `x`, `t`, `rd2` or `tmp`. Loop indices
  (`i`, `line`) are fine when the meaning is obvious.
- Official gbatek register and field names are allowed (`DISPCNT`, `BG0CNT`, `IE`, `IF`, `CPSR`, `Rd`, `Rn`),
  each with a short plain-English comment where it is defined, e.g. `const DISPCNT: u32 = 0x000; // display control`.
- Every non-obvious function gets a one-line doc comment naming the gbatek section it implements, e.g.
  `/// Barrel shifter for data-processing operand 2 (gbatek: ARM Opcodes: Data Processing (ALU)).`
- Prefer small readable functions over clever one-liners. Split a long `match` arm or a dense bit-twiddling
  expression into a named helper.

## Ownership
- Only edit the files your task owns (see the ownership tables in PLAN.md).
- Shared files (`src/lib.rs`, `src/gba.rs`, `src/bus.rs`, `src/io.rs`, `src/irq.rs`, `src/scheduler.rs`,
  `Cargo.toml`) are changed only by the integrator (the executor session). If you need a contract
  change, say so in your report instead of making it.

## Git
- Remote: https://github.com/Rohan-Jalil/gba-eval-trial-rohan. Never push; the human pushes.
- Author and committer: Rohan Jalil <[REDACTED:email]>. This is set in this repo's git config;
  do not override it.
- Use Conventional Commits: `type(scope): summary`, for example `feat(cpu): add ARM data-processing ops`,
  `fix(ppu): wrap affine BG coordinates`, `test(timer): cascade overflow`, `docs(notes): phase 1 decisions`,
  `chore(results): phase 1 milestone`. Scopes: cpu, arm, thumb, bus, io, irq, ppu, apu, dma, timer,
  keypad, cart, abi, scripts, plan, notes, results.
- Commit after every meaningful step (a working instruction group, a passing test, a merged branch),
  not one large commit per phase.
- Worker agents commit on their own branch. Only the integrator merges into `main` (`git merge --no-ff`).

## Logging
- `NOTES.md`: add an entry for every decision or change of approach (date, what, why), and for every
  phase record which agents ran and on which model. The integrator writes the agent/model rows.
- `TIMELOG.md` belongs to the human. Agents never edit it.
- Milestones: `scripts/grade-full.sh <phase> "<note>"` saves `results/milestones/<phase>/`. Commit that
  folder and `scores.tsv`. All other `results/` output stays ignored.

## Before you report done
1. `cargo test` passes.
2. `cargo build --release --lib --target wasm32-unknown-unknown` succeeds.
3. `scripts/grade-subset.sh target/wasm32-unknown-unknown/release/gba_emu.wasm <name> <your tests> <smoke set>`.
   Report the per-test scores, and never lower a smoke-set score without saying so.
4. Your work is committed on your branch, and your report lists the commits.

(15bit). The data stream repeats after 7Fh (7bit) or 7FFFh (15bit) steps.





  
  GBA Sound Channel A and B - DMA Sound

The GBA contains two DMA sound channels (A and B), each allowing to replay
digital sound (signed 8bit data, ie. -128..+127). Data can be transferred from
INTERNAL memory (not sure if EXTERNAL memory works also ?) to FIFO by using DMA
channel 1 or 2, the sample rate is generated by using one of the Timers.

40000A0h - FIFO_A_L - Sound A FIFO, Data 0 and Data 1 (W)
40000A2h - FIFO_A_H - Sound A FIFO, Data 2 and Data 3 (W)
These two registers may receive 32bit (4 bytes) of audio data (Data 0-3, Data 0
being located in least significant byte which is replayed first).
Internally, the capacity of the FIFO is 8 x 32bit (32 bytes), allowing to
buffer a small amount of samples. As the name says (First In First Out), oldest
data is replayed first.

40000A4h - FIFO_B_L - Sound B FIFO, Data 0 and Data 1 (W)
40000A6h - FIFO_B_H - Sound B FIFO, Data 2 and Data 3 (W)
Same as above, for Sound B.

Initializing DMA-Sound Playback
- Select Timer 0 or 1 in SOUNDCNT_H control register.
- Clear the FIFO.
- Manually write a sample byte to the FIFO.
- Initialize transfer mode for DMA 1 or 2.
- Initialize DMA Sound settings in sound control register.
- Start the timer.

DMA-Sound Playback Procedure
The pseudo-procedure below is automatically repeated.

  If Timer overflows then
    Move 8bit data from FIFO to sound circuit.
    If FIFO contains only 4 x 32bits (16 bytes) then
      Request more data per DMA
      Receive 4 x 32bit (16 bytes) per DMA
    Endif
  Endif

This playback mechanism will be repeated forever, regardless of the actual
length of the sample buffer.

Synchronizing Sample Buffers
The buffer-end may be determined by counting sound Timer IRQs (each sample
byte), or sound DMA IRQs (each 16th sample byte). Both methods would require a
lot of CPU time (IRQ processing), and both would fail if interrupts are
disabled for a longer period.
Better solutions would be to synchronize the sample rate/buffer length with
V-blanks, or to use a second timer (in count up/slave mode) which produces an
IRQ after the desired number of samples.

The Sample Rate
The GBA hardware does internally re-sample all sound output to 32.768kHz
(default SOUNDBIAS setting). It'd thus do not make much sense to use higher
DMA/Timer rates. Best re-sampling accuracy can be gained by using DMA/Timer
rates of 32.768kHz, 16.384kHz, or 8.192kHz (ie. fragments of the physical
output rate).





  
  GBA Sound Control Registers

4000080h - SOUNDCNT_L (NR50, NR51) - Channel L/R Volume/Enable (R/W)

  Bit        Expl.
  0-2   R/W  Sound 1-4 Master Volume RIGHT (0-7)
  3     -    Not used
  4-6   R/W  Sound 1-4 Master Volume LEFT (0-7)
  7     -    Not used
  8-11  R/W  Sound 1-4 Enable Flags RIGHT (each Bit 8-11, 0=Disable, 1=Enable)
  12-15 R/W  Sound 1-4 Enable Flags LEFT (each Bit 12-15, 0=Disable, 1=Enable)


4000082h - SOUNDCNT_H (GBA only) - DMA Sound Control/Mixing (R/W)

  Bit        Expl.
  0-1   R/W  Sound # 1-4 Volume   (0=25%, 1=50%, 2=100%, 3=Prohibited)
  2     R/W  DMA Sound A Volume   (0=50%, 1=100%)
  3     R/W  DMA Sound B Volume   (0=50%, 1=100%)
  4-7   -    Not used
  8     R/W  DMA Sound A Enable RIGHT (0=Disable, 1=Enable)
  9     R/W  DMA Sound A Enable LEFT  (0=Disable, 1=Enable)
  10    R/W  DMA Sound A Timer Select (0=Timer 0, 1=Timer 1)
  11    W?   DMA Sound A Reset FIFO   (1=Reset)
  12    R/W  DMA Sound B Enable RIGHT (0=Disable, 1=Enable)
  13    R/W  DMA Sound B Enable LEFT  (0=Disable, 1=Enable)
  14    R/W  DMA Sound B Timer Select (0=Timer 0, 1=Timer 1)
  15    W?   DMA Sound B Reset FIFO   (1=Reset)


4000084h - SOUNDCNT_X (NR52) - Sound on/off (R/W)
Bits 0-3 are automatically set when starting sound output, and are
automatically cleared when a sound ends. (Ie. when the length expires, as far
as length is enabled. The bits are NOT reset when an volume envelope ends.)

  Bit        Expl.
  0     R    Sound 1 ON flag (Read Only)
  1     R    Sound 2 ON flag (Read Only)
  2     R    Sound 3 ON flag (Read Only)
  3     R    Sound 4 ON flag (Read Only)
  4-6   -    Not used
  7     R/W  PSG/FIFO Master Enable (0=Disable, 1=Enable) (Read/Write)

The GBA contains two DMA sound channels (A and B), each allowing to replay

buffer a small amount of samples. As the name says (First In First Out), oldest

Initializing DMA-Sound Playback
- Select Timer 0 or 1 in SOUNDCNT_H control register.
- Clear the FIFO.
- Manually write a sample byte to the FIFO.
- Initialize transfer mode for DMA 1 or 2.
- Initialize DMA Sound settings in sound control register.
- Start the timer.

DMA-Sound Playback Procedure
The pseudo-procedure below is automatically repeated.

  If Timer overflows then
    Move 8bit data from FIFO to sound circuit.
    If FIFO contains only 4 x 32bits (16 bytes) then
      Request more data per DMA
      Receive 4 x 32bit (16 bytes) per DMA
    Endif
  Endif

This playback mechanism will be repeated forever, regardless of the actual
length of the sample buffer.

The buffer-end may be determined by counting sound Timer IRQs (each sample
byte), or sound DMA IRQs (each 16th sample byte). Both methods would require a
lot of CPU time (IRQ processing), and both would fail if interrupts are
disabled for a longer period.
Better solutions would be to synchronize the sample rate/buffer length with
V-blanks, or to use a second timer (in count up/slave mode) which produces an
IRQ after the desired number of samples.

The GBA hardware does internally re-sample all sound output to 32.768kHz

DMA/Timer rates. Best re-sampling accuracy can be gained by using DMA/Timer
rates of 32.768kHz, 16.384kHz, or 8.192kHz (ie. fragments of the physical

FIFO A/B and the mixer are in. Celeste audio went from 0.0 to 0.886 and piugba from 0.0 to 0.684. The smoke set did not regress. All 116 `cargo test` tests pass, the wasm release build succeeds, and both commits are on branch `phase4/apu-fifo-mixer`, not pushed.

## 1. What I built and the commits

- `c04db04 fix(apu): halve DAC to i16 scale to match reference level and avoid clipping`
- `9070d5f feat(apu): direct sound FIFOs, mixer and SOUNDBIAS DAC output`

**`/var/www/html/test-projects/gba-trial/gba-emu/.claude/worktrees/agent-a4ec101f887cf580c/src/apu/fifo.rs`**
- Each FIFO holds 32 bytes. Writes to FIFO_A/FIFO_B (0x0A0-0x0A7) push the bytes the write mask selects, low byte first, so 8-, 16- and 32-bit writes all work.
- Each timer overflow moves one byte to the output, and that sample is held until the next overflow. If the FIFO is empty, the last sample keeps playing.
- After each pop it reports a refill when 16 bytes or fewer remain. The reset bit empties the FIFO and sets its output to 0.

**`/var/www/html/test-projects/gba-trial/gba-emu/.claude/worktrees/agent-a4ec101f887cf580c/src/apu/mod.rs`**
- **Timer overflows:** `on_timer_overflow` pops from each FIFO whose SOUNDCNT_H timer select matches, but only while the master enable is on. It returns the refill mask.
- **PSG mixing:** each channel level (-15..15) is multiplied by the SOUNDCNT_L master volume + 1. It is then reduced for the SOUNDCNT_H ratio (25/50/100%) and added left and right according to the enable bits.
- **FIFO mixing:** each FIFO sample is multiplied by 4 at 100% volume or by 2 at 50%, giving the +/-0x200 range gbatek describes.
- **DAC output:** the sum plus the bias is clipped to 0..0x3FF. The low bits the selected resolution cannot output are dropped. The bias is then subtracted and the result shifted left 5 to give the i16 sample. If the master enable is off, the output is silence.
- **SOUNDCNT_H:** the FIFO reset bits (11 and 15) act on write and are not stored.
- **SOUNDCNT_X:** reads return the stored bit 7 plus `psg.active_channels()`. When bit 7 goes from 1 to 0, it calls `psg.power_off()` and clears SOUNDCNT_L.
- **Sample rate:** `sample_rate()` and the sample count per frame follow 32768 << SOUNDBIAS bits 14-15. Each sample takes exactly 16777216 / rate cycles (512, 256, 128 or 64), so the count never drifts. On the dev ROMs, 300 frames gave exactly 164587 samples at 32768 Hz.
- **Unit tests:** FIFO byte order, byte writes, refill threshold and reset; FIFO-to-mixer output; the sample count at 262 kHz; DAC clipping.

## 2. Scores

| Test | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| celeste-gameplay audio | 0.0 | 0.8857 (0.8858 at shift 6) |
| piugba-gameplay audio | 0.0 | 0.6840 (0.6799 at shift 6) |
| aw-arm-alu, aw-thumb-alu, memory, timer-reload, dma-priority | video 1.0 | 1.0 |
| tonc-snd1 | video 0.9917, audio 0.0 | 0.9917, 0.0 |

- tonc-snd1 audio stays at 0 because the PSG is still a stub; that is the PSG worker's file.
- I ran the full smoke set at shift 6 and only the two graded games after the shift-5 commit. The shift only changes audio level, so it cannot affect the video-only smoke tests.
- Both dev ROMs produce non-silent audio.

## 3. Unfinished work, guesses and contract changes

- **Output level:** the shift of 5 came from comparing against the reference WAVs, which were about 2x quieter than ours. Celeste and piugba both showed the same ratio, so it is not tuned to one game.
- **piugba length:** our output is 957 samples (about 1.7 frames) longer than the reference. The loudness over time otherwise tracks the reference closely, so the offset probably comes from frame or boot alignment outside my files.
- **Where gbatek is unclear, I guessed:**
  - Bytes written to a full FIFO are dropped.
  - An empty FIFO keeps playing its last sample.
  - FIFOs only pop while the master enable is on.
  - Refill requests go out whatever the left/right enable bits are, so an empty FIFO B on the same timer also gets one. The DMA ignores it unless a channel targets FIFO B.
  - SOUNDCNT_H ratio value 3 ("prohibited") is treated as 100%.
  - PSG register writes are not blocked while the master enable is off; gbatek doesn't say they should be.
- **Contract changes:** none needed.

## 4. Decisions for NOTES.md

- 2026-11-05: mixer works in gbatek's DAC units (each FIFO +/-0x200, each PSG channel about +/-0x80, plus bias, clipped to 10 bits, low bits dropped per resolution). Why: it follows the "Max Output Levels" section directly.
- 2026-11-05: i16 sample = (DAC value - bias) << 5. Subtracting the bias makes silence 0 even when a game sets bias 0. Shift 5 matches the reference WAV level, which was about 2x below shift 6, and avoids clipping.
- 2026-11-05: refill request is raised when a FIFO holds 16 bytes or fewer after a pop, for every FIFO on the overflowing timer. Why: gbatek says "only 4 x 32bits"; the DMA filters by destination address.
